objectives.description: auto exits 2 with marker + remedy test
ocrmypdf-dependent real OCR round-trip test (skips with warning if absent)
exit-3 QUALITY GATE FAILED prefix + remedy line test
literature-ingest.sh bucketing coverage (needs-OCR vs marker-free hard-failure)

approaches_tried.approach: Build the image-only fixture from a plain fitz.draw_rect() shape with no rendered text
approaches_tried.reason: no OCR-recognizable content at all -- confirms zero-text-layer but ocrmypdf also correctly finds nothing, so the LITERATURE_CONVERTER=ocr round-trip test could never observe real text recovery

approaches_tried.approach: Point LITERATURE_PYENV_DIR at a nonexistent-but-writable scratch directory to force the primary tier unavailable
approaches_tried.reason: literature-pyenv-provision.sh happily auto-provisions a fresh venv there (uv + network both available in this environment), silently restoring the primary tier and defeating the forced-unavailable premise; replaced with an unwritable (chmod 000) parent directory, which makes `uv venv` fail deterministically

approaches_tried.approach: Assert the full '=== Ingestion Summary ===' block for the marker-free exit-2 ingest scenario
approaches_tried.reason: when PROCESSED==0 (the sole file in the batch hard-fails), literature-ingest.sh takes its early All-files-failed branch and exits 3 BEFORE ever reaching the summary block -- replaced with an assertion against the early-exit aggregate stderr log line instead

deviations.description: Fixed a pre-existing gap in literature-convert.sh's exit-2 empty-output check (not originally scoped to any single phase's task list, but directly blocking Phase 1-3's real-world efficacy)
deviations.reason: Discovered while building/verifying this phase's image-only fixture: the mandatory fallback tier's extract_blocks_mode()/extract_dict_mode() emit a literal '[figure omitted]' placeholder for every image XObject block, so a genuinely image-only PDF (built the standard way, an embedded image rather than vector-only drawing) does NOT produce an empty string and was silently succeeding with a useless one-line '.md' instead of hitting the exit-2 NO TEXT LAYER path -- defeating the entire premise of Phases 1-3 for the realistic case of an operator without a provisioned pymupdf4llm venv. Added a small _is_placeholder_only() helper (literature-convert.sh) that treats placeholder-only content as empty for this check; verified via full suite + two targeted revert-and-confirm-failure checks.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- extended Phase 1's exit-2 empty-output check to also catch placeholder-only fallback-tier output; see phase-4-progress.json findings)*

findings: pymupdf4llm's own force_text=True default (pre-existing, unrelated to this task) makes the PRIMARY tier silently recover text via its own internal Tesseract call whenever a page has no text layer and system tesseract is on PATH -- confirmed with the image-only fixture under LITERATURE_CONVERTER=auto with the venv provisioned. This is a DIFFERENT code path than the ocrmypdf CLI this task adds; the 'auto never invokes ocrmypdf' guarantee holds regardless. Phase 4's auto-exits-2 test forces the primary tier unavailable (via an unwritable LITERATURE_PYENV_DIR parent) to get a deterministic assertion, matching how auto degrades on any machine without a provisioned venv.

SEPARATE AND MORE SIGNIFICANT: literature-convert.sh's mandatory fallback tier (the one every operator without a provisioned primary-tier venv actually uses) does NOT treat a genuinely image-only PDF as empty output on its own -- it emits a non-empty '[figure omitted]' placeholder for the image block, which passed the pre-existing `not content.strip()` check and the quality gate (page-coverage check is bypassed when the source itself has 0 extractable words). Fixed as part of this phase (see deviations); without this fix the entire task's exit-2/needs-OCR/LITERATURE_CONVERTER=ocr chain would never trigger for a real scanned PDF converted via the fallback tier.
